arxiv-2107-07017.title: The Traveling Salesman Theorem for Jordan Curves in Hilbert Space
arxiv-2107-07017.creator: Jared Krandel
arxiv-2107-07017.description: Abstract Given a metric space X X , an Analyst’s Traveling Salesman Theorem for X X gives a quantitative relationship between the length of a shortest curve containing any subset E ⊆ X E\subseteq X and a multi-scale sum measuring the “flatness” of E E .

arxiv-2206-03161.title: Erik P. Verlinde
arxiv-2206-03161.description: Abstract We discuss whether black hole entropy counts short or long range microstates in quantum gravity. In brick wall and induced gravity models the entropy arises due to short distance correlations across the event horizon cut off at the Planck length. However, the energy of these short range degrees of freedom is too high compared to the black hole energy.

arxiv-2212-07566.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Neelofar Neelofar, Aldeida Aleti. Ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles (AVs) is of utmost importance, and testing them in simulated environments is a safer option than conducting in-field operational tests. However, generating an exhaustive test suite to identify critical test scenarios is computationally expensive as the representation of each test is complex and contains various dynamic and static features, such as the AV under test, road participants (vehicles, pedestrians, and static obstacles), environmental factors (weather and light), and the road’s structural features (lanes, turns,

arxiv-2306-02905.title: INNER AND PARTIAL NON-DEGENERACY OF MIXED FUNCTIONS
arxiv-2306-02905.creator: Benjamin Bode, Eder L. Sanchez Quiceno
arxiv-2306-02905.description: Abstract Mixed polynomials f : ℂ 2 → ℂ f:\mathbb{C}^{2}\to\mathbb{C} are polynomial maps in complex variables u u and v v as well as their complex conjugates u ¯ \bar{u} and v ¯ \bar{v} . They are therefore identical to the set of real polynomial maps from ℝ 4 \mathbb{R}^{4} to ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} .

arxiv-2312-00917.title: Closing the feedback-feeding loop of the radio galaxy 3C 84
arxiv-2312-00917.creator: Tom Oosterloo 1,2, Raffaella Morganti 1,2 & Suma Murthy 3
arxiv-2312-00917.description: Abstract Gas accretion by a galaxy’s central super massive black hole (SMBH) and the resultant energetic feedback by the accreting active galactic nucleus (AGN) on the gas in and around a galaxy, are two tightly intertwined but competing processes that play a crucial role in the evolution of galaxies.

arxiv-2403-01814.title: Rotation effect on the deconfinement phase transition in holographic QCD
arxiv-2403-01814.creator: Jia-Hao Wang, Sheng-Qin Feng
arxiv-2403-01814.description: Abstract Abstract: The impact of rotation on the deconfinement phase transition under the EM system of the soft and the hard wall models in holographic quantum chromodynamics is studied in this paper. The metric by cylindrical coordinates with rotation is introduced into the system to calculate the Hawking temperature.

arxiv-2405-04060.title: Simulation of Gacs’ Automaton
arxiv-2405-04060.creator: Atsushi Masumori*, Lana Sinapayen*, Takashi Ikegami
arxiv-2405-04060.description: Abstract Peter Gacs proposed a one-dimensional cellular automaton capable of a robust self-reproduction. Because the automaton is exceptionally large and complicated, very few people have ever succeeded in simulating it on a computer or analyzing its behavior. Here we demonstrate a partial simulation of Gacs’ automaton (of Gray’s version), discussing its robustness.

arxiv-2406-04324.title: SF-V: Single Forward Video Generation Model
arxiv-2406-04324.creator: Zhixing Zhang, Yanyu Li, Yushu Wu, Yanwu Xu, Anil Kag, Ivan Skorokhodov, Willi Menapace, Aliaksandr Siarohin, Junli Cao, Dimitris Metaxas, Sergey Tulyakov, Jian Ren
arxiv-2406-04324.description: Abstract Diffusion-based video generation models have demonstrated remarkable success in obtaining high-fidelity videos through the iterative denoising process. However, these models require multiple denoising steps during sampling, resulting in high computational costs. In this work, we propose a novel approach to obtain single -step video generation models by leveraging adversarial training to fine-tune pre-trained video diffusion models.

arxiv-2408-16857.title: Modeling offensive content detection for TikTok
arxiv-2408-16857.creator: 1 st Kasper Cools, 2 nd Gideon Mailette de Buy Wenniger, 3 rd Clara Maathuis
arxiv-2408-16857.description: Abstract The advent of social media transformed interpersonal communication and information consumption processes. This digital landscape accommodates user intentions, also resulting in an increase of offensive language and harmful behavior. Concurrently, social media platforms collect vast datasets comprising user-generated content and behavioral information.

arxiv-2505-23215.title: Trajectory Generator Matching for Time Series
arxiv-2505-23215.creator: T. Jahn, J. Chemseddine, P. Hagemann, C. Wald, G. Steidl
arxiv-2505-23215.description: Abstract Accurately modeling time-continuous stochastic processes from irregular observations remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we leverage ideas from generative modeling of image data to push the boundary of time series generation. For this, we find new generators of SDEs and jump processes, inspired by trajectory flow matching, that have the marginal distributions of the time series of interest.

arxiv-2506-01230.title: Stress-Testing ML Pipelines with Adversarial Data Corruption
arxiv-2506-01230.creator: Jiongli Zhu, Geyang Xu, Felipe Lorenzi, Boris Glavic, Babak Salimi
arxiv-2506-01230.description: Abstract . Structured data-quality issues—such as missing values correlated with demographics, culturally biased labels, or systemic selection biases—routinely degrade the reliability of machine-learning pipelines. Regulators now increasingly demand evidence that high-stakes systems can withstand these realistic, interdependent errors, yet current robustness evaluations typically use random or overly simplistic corruptions, leaving worst-case scenarios unexplored.

arxiv-2509-01606.title: Testing the assumptions about the geometry of sentence embedding spaces: the cosine measure need not apply
arxiv-2509-01606.creator: Vivi Nastase, Paola Merlo
arxiv-2509-01606.description: Abstract Transformer models learn to encode and decode an input text, and produce contextual token embeddings as a side-effect. The mapping from language into the embedding space maps words expressing similar concepts onto points that are close in the space.

arxiv-2511-01793.title: Stochastic Multigrid Method for Blind Ptychographic Phase Retrieval
arxiv-2511-01793.creator: Borong Zhang, Junjing Deng, Yi Jiang, Zichao Wendy Di
arxiv-2511-01793.description: Abstract We present eMAGPIE (extended Multilevel–Adaptive–Guided Ptychographic Iterative Engine), a stochastic multigrid method for blind ptychographic phase retrieval that jointly recovers the object and the probe. We recast the task as the iterative minimization of a quadratic surrogate that majorizes the exit-wave misfit.

pmc-10601473.title: Unraveling the Bürgi-Dunitz Angle with Precision: The Power of a Two-Dimensional Energy Decomposition Analysis
pmc-10601473.creator: Israel Fernández, F Matthias Bickelhaupt, Dennis Svatunek
pmc-10601473.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Understanding the geometrical preferences in chemical reactions is crucial for advancing the field of organic chemistry and improving synthetic strategies. One such preference, the Bürgi-Dunitz angle, is central to nucleophilic addition reactions involving carbonyl groups. This study successfully employs a novel two-dimensional Distortion-Interaction/Activation-Strain Model in combination with a two-dimensional Energy Decomposition Analysis to investigate the origins of the Bürgi-Dunitz angle in the addition reaction of CN– to (CH3)2C=O.

pmc-11500311.description: The regulatory protein NsrR, a member of the Rrf2 protein superfamily, plays a major role in the cellular response to nitrosative stress in many benign and pathogenic bacteria. pmc-11508786.title: Race, Sex, and Ejection Fraction-Based Differences in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) Risk Prediction
pmc-11508786.creator: Michel Chedid El Helou, Mohak Gupta, Muzna Hussain, Mazen Hanna, Vanessa Blumer, Preethi William, Milind Y. Desai, Bryan Q. Abadie, Lauren Ives, W. H. Wilson Tang, Wael A. Jaber, Patrick Collier, Trejeeve Martyn

Although a previously validated score has shown promise in predicting PYP scan positivity among patients with HFpEF, further evaluation in diverse cohorts is necessary.

pmc-11715351.description: BackgroundHippocampal Sclerosis of aging (HS) refers to age‐related selective neuronal loss and gliosis in hippocampal cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) and subiculum that is out of proportion to tau pathology in Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). HS is related to cognitive decline and memory impairments separately from other neurodegenerative pathologies.

pmc-12575147.title: Why mindfulness matters in musculoskeletal therapies: a narrative review
pmc-12575147.creator: Peter Bablis, Ryan R. Day, Sophia Bablis, Henry Pollard
pmc-12575147.description: This narrative review explores the integration of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) into musculoskeletal (MSK) care, based on the premise that addressing the mind–body interface can enhance patient outcomes. First, we outline how chronic stress affects twelve physiological systems and contributes to the onset and persistence of MSK conditions.

pmc-12606041.creator: Nikhil Bellamkonda, Anne Naumer, Luke O. Buchmann, Hilary C. McCrary, Mana Espahbodi, Neil S. Patel

pmc-13437239.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis does not influence manufacturing of Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-Cells
pmc-13437239.creator: Simon M Krauß, Konstantin Weibl, Enrica Bach, Mandy Brückner, Anne Weigert, Theresa Tumewu, Elena Ruschpler, Gunhild Vogtmann, Sandra Hoffmann, Olaf Penack, Martin Janz, Raymund Buhmann, Reinhard Henschler, Lars Bullinger, Ulrich Keller, Sebastian Schwind, Maximilian Merz, Madlen Jentzsch, Georg-Nik
pmc-13437239.description: Treatment with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells has proven as a highly effective option for treatment of patients with lymphoproliferative diseases and plasma cell dyscrasia. Tisagenlecleucel (tisa-cel; Novartis AG, Basel, Switzerland) is approved for treatment of patients with large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia and follicular lymphoma after two previous treatment lines [1].

pmc-13561437.title: Supporting the Learning of Visual Perception Skills in Cytology Through a Computational Tool: Development and Evaluation Study
pmc-13561437.creator: Breno Nunes de Sena Keller, Mariana T Rezende, Renata RR Oliveira, Cristina RP Costa, Claudia M Carneiro, Andrea G Campos
pmc-13561437.description: BackgroundAdvances in hardware and software have transformed how users perform activities across various domains by integrating technology in ways that enhance task execution. In education, these processes facilitate pedagogical innovation and learning through diverse interaction models, such as web systems, augmented or virtual reality, and mobile devices. An example of these approaches occurs in the context of cytopathology.

pmc-13602673.title: A novel Au-Se nanoplatform for co-delivery of cGAMP and acriflavine synergizes with photothermal therapy to enhance anti-tumor immunity via STING activation and HIF-1α inhibition
pmc-13602673.creator: Yuanyuan Cui, Yonghui Liang, Huixin Yang, Xudong Wang, Yanjiao Zhang, Guilong Zhang, Renhui Zhan
pmc-13602673.description: Activating the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is a potent strategy for promoting tumor vascular normalization and enhancing cancer immunotherapy. However, the poor metabolic stability of classical STING agonists limits their clinical translation. Herein, we engineered a self-assembled Au-Se nanoplatform (AAC) for the co-delivery of the STING agonist cyclic 2’,3’-GMP-AMP (cGAMP) and the hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) inhibitor acriflavine (Acf).

pmc-13609287.title: Efficient CO2 Activation Mediated by Triplet Pnictinidenes
pmc-13609287.creator: Zheng-Feng Zhang, Ming-Der Su
pmc-13609287.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The present investigation delineates the mechanistic landscape governing the [1 + 2] cycloaddition of CO2 with triplet monomeric pnictinidenes ([G15–Rea]3; G15 = Group 15 element) and identifies the principal energetic factors controlling their periodic reactivity. The computed potential-energy profiles support a stepwise mechanism in which cycloaddition is initiated on the triplet potential-energy surface through [G15–TS]3, followed by a singlet–triplet surface-crossing event at [G15–T/S] and subsequent relaxation to the singlet heterocyclic products [G15–Prod]1.
